original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Exhibit a non-coordinate eight-term one-sided mask-only completion with COPY71 versus COPY72 in the same frame on the fixed 93-line first-failure unit of PR1609, and an all-pairs COPY63 comparator on that same unit.
scope_change_reason: The assigned card asks for a legal complete supplier invoice. This side result isolates the separate-term binary pairing-rank diagnostic at PR1609's first-failure boundary. The coordinate perturbation census belongs to the earlier public claim #discussioncomment-19530120 and is omitted here.
bottleneck_link: A mask-only identity can lower a fixed-frame COPY bill without beating another all-pairs frame. The two explicit constructions distinguish those comparisons before spending effort on unpriced physical acquisition, restoration and delivery.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified non-coordinate completion and explicit same-unit comparator. Do not optimize frames further or construct a physical supplier.
evidence: RESULT.json is generated by verify.py and binds the verifier and predecessor certificate hashes. Exact rational checks cover every entry of the two new constructions and the same-frame baseline. Every support pairing rank is computed by bitset and dense F2 elimination. The one-sided ranks are [8,9,9,9,9,9,9,9]; the all-pairs ranks are [7,8,7,8,8,8,8,9].
